subplans.title: Accounts, sessions and server-side permissions
subplans.outcome: Invited accounts with hashed passwords and revocable server sessions replace the shared APP_PASSWORD; every page and API of the pilot checks the permission it needs on the server; roles and the three access plans are sets of permissions; the local no-restrictions flag cannot be enabled in production; the first administrator is created by a one-off command.
acceptance_criteria: Migration 037 applies on an empty isolated schema and again on an already migrated one without error, creates the account, role, session, link and sign-in attempt tables, and seeds exactly the five system roles.
Every page.tsx and route.ts under src/app matches exactly one entry of the route permission map, and the test fails naming any file that matches none or several.

The five system roles hold exactly the permissions of the owner's table: Plan 1 chat, balloon counter and catalogue; Plan 2 adds costs and the decorations explorer; Plan 3 adds the Taller 3D; Empleado interno adds everyone's projects, AI spend and internal tools; Administrador adds users, roles and text corrections.

An administrator's invitation creates an invited account with a single-use link valid seven days; activating it sets a password of at least eight characters, records the data-notice version and date, and a second use of the same link is refused.
Signing in with the right email and password of an active account creates a session; a wrong password, an unknown email and a deactivated account all get the same generic refusal.
After five failed sign-ins for one email within fifteen minutes that email is refused for fifteen minutes even with the right password, and other emails are unaffected.
Deactivating, deleting or changing the role of the last active Administrador is refused; deleting an account removes its personal data rows.
npm run cuentas:primer-admin creates an invited Administrador for the given email and prints its activation link once, and refuses without changes when an active Administrador already exists.
Deactivating an account, changing its password or signing out ends its sessions on the next request, and a role change applies on the next request without signing in again.

Without a valid session a page request redirects to /login keeping the path and an API request gets 401 JSON; with a session lacking the mapped permission a page shows the no-access page and an API gets 403 JSON.
A cookie or form built from the old APP_PASSWORD no longer grants access, and no code path reads APP_PASSWORD.

With AUTH_LOCAL_SIN_RESTRICCIONES=1 under next dev, a request from 127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost runs as the Administrador local account without signing in, and a request from any other address must sign in.
With AUTH_LOCAL_SIN_RESTRICCIONES set, next build, next start, a Vercel environment and the ai-api deployment refuse to start with an error naming the variable.
Every API route handler outside the public and own-auth exceptions calls the permission guard with the permission the map assigns to its path before doing any work.

Against a production build started with next start on the REQ-021 test database, one Plan 1, one Plan 3, one Empleado interno and one Administrador account each reach exactly their mapped pages and APIs, a deactivated account loses access on its next request, and the old shared password is refused.
An independent security audit of SP-1 records every confirmed defect with the task that must redo it in the SP-1 findings ledger, and the ledger has no open critical or high finding.

acceptance_criteria: Generating a new invitation or reset link for an account invalidates every older unused link of the same kind for that account, and a custom role with no permission is refused with ROL_SIN_PERMISOS.

Deleting an account that owns any row of a table registered as account work is refused with CUENTA_CON_TRABAJO and changes nothing, while deleting an account without saved work removes it and keeps its AI spend rows without personal data.

On /login a person signs in with email and password; a wrong password, an unknown email, a deactivated account and a locked email all show the same message, which always adds that after several failures one must wait fifteen minutes, and success returns to the requested page or the first area the role allows, or Mi cuenta when the role has none of them.

Opening an invitation link shows the invited name and email, asks for a password of at least eight characters twice and shows the data notice in the browser language with an accept checkbox, activation is impossible without accepting, and after activating the person lands signed in on the first tool their role allows; a used or expired link shows a message to ask the administrator for a new one.
When the notice version changes, a signed-in person must accept the new version before any other page opens.
Every signed-in page shows an account menu with the person's name and role, Mi cuenta and sign out, and Mi cuenta changes the password by asking for the current one.
An administrator invites a person by name, email, optional company and role, and gets the single-use link once with a copy button; an email already registered is refused with a clear message.

An administrator changes an account's role, deactivates and reactivates it, generates a reset link and deletes an account without saved work after typing its email, and the screen explains why the last administrator or an account with saved work cannot be deleted.

An administrator creates and edits a custom role by name and permission checkboxes grouped by tool, sees the five system roles read-only with their permissions, and cannot delete a role that still has accounts.
The account and role administration APIs refuse anyone without the users or roles permission with 403 and accept only same-origin requests with validated bodies.
The data notice exists in Spanish and English with a version number, its bracketed placeholders are still marked for legal review, and accepting stores the version and date on the account.
